## Noe Cafe, my go-to for a meeting and an easy coffee in Noe Valley

> Noe Cafe on the Sanchez Slow Street, Noe Valley: a chill spot for meetings and coffee. Get the Breakfast Sandwich and avocado toast; beer later in the day.

- **Restaurant:** Noe Cafe
- **City:** San Francisco
- **Neighborhood:** Noe Valley
- **Cuisine:** Coffee shop · Cafe
- **Must order:** Breakfast Sandwich
- **Address:** 1299 Sanchez St (at 26th St), San Francisco, CA 94114
- **Website:** https://noecafe.com/
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Noe+Cafe+1299+Sanchez+St+San+Francisco+CA+94114
- **Reviewed:** 2026-10-13
- **Author:** Christian Van Der Henst (Cvander)
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/noe-cafe
- **City guide:** San Francisco: https://www.cookfoodie.com/wishlist/san-francisco

### Review

It's a really cool coffee shop in Noe Valley, on the Sanchez Slow Street, very child and dog friendly.

I love it. They have two branches, the other one in Mission Bay, but the one I really like is Noe Cafe in Noe Valley. They have a nice parklet, so you can really grab your coffee outside. They also have some inside tables that aren't always available, but the vibe is pretty good.

Occasionally during the week they bring a guy who sells tacos, wearing a big taco hat. It's the place where you hang out when you live in the Noe Valley area, but it's also visited by a lot of tech people and VCs.

I really recommend their sandwiches and their toast. The avocado toast is really good, and I usually get the breakfast sandwich. Other than the different coffees, they also have a selection of kombuchas, and they have a liquor license, so if you go a little later in the day you can also grab a beer. It's a great spot for a beer, and whenever there are festivities on Sanchez, the community and the ambience are really good.

Some other friends always say it's a very chill place and a great place for meetings, and I agree. It's my go-to place to have a meeting, or just to enjoy an easy coffee in Noe Valley.

Noe Cafe, the best place to have a coffee, chill and hang out with your friends in Noe Valley.

### What to order

- **Breakfast Sandwich:** My usual. Brioche bun, eggs, cheddar and arugula.
- **Avocado Toast:** Really good.
- **Coffee:** Grab it and sit outside in the parklet.

### Locations

- **Noe Cafe — Noe Valley** (Noe Valley, San Francisco): 1299 Sanchez St (at 26th St), San Francisco, CA 94114. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Noe+Cafe+1299+Sanchez+St+San+Francisco+CA+94114. The original, and the one I like. On the Sanchez Slow Street. Mon–Wed 7am–5pm, Thu–Sun 7am–6pm.
- **Noe Cafe — Mission Bay / Dogpatch** (Mission Bay / Dogpatch, San Francisco): 601 18th St, San Francisco, CA 94107. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Noe+Cafe+601+18th+St+San+Francisco+CA+94107. Across from Crane Cove Park.

### If you're visiting Noe Cafe

#### Where is Noe Cafe?

1299 Sanchez St at 26th St, Noe Valley, on the Sanchez Slow Street. There's a parklet outside and some tables inside.

#### What should I order at Noe Cafe?

I usually get the Breakfast Sandwich. The avocado toast is really good too. Besides coffee, they have kombuchas, and beer later in the day.

#### What are Noe Cafe's hours?

Mon–Wed 7am–5pm, Thu–Sun 7am–6pm.

### Photos

- Tacos from the taco guy: https://www.cookfoodie.com/img/reviews/noe-cafe-tacos.jpg

## La Espiga: My favorite place, it really felt like home

> La Espiga, a family-run pintxos bar in San Sebastián: Tortillita with truffles, rollito de jamón, croquetas, and wine by the glass. Open 10 AM to 10 PM.

- **Restaurant:** La Espiga
- **City:** San Sebastián
- **Neighborhood:** Centro
- **Cuisine:** Basque pintxos
- **Rating:** 5/5
- **Must order:** Tortillita with trufa
- **Address:** San Martzial Kalea, 48, 20006 Donostia / San Sebastián, Spain
- **Phone:** +34 943 421 423
- **Website:** https://www.laespigabar.com/
- **Instagram:** https://www.instagram.com/granbarlaespiga/
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=La+Espiga+San+Martzial+Kalea+48+Donostia+San+Sebastian
- **Reviewed:** 2026-09-26
- **Author:** Christian Van Der Henst (Cvander)
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/la-espiga
- **City guide:** San Sebastián: https://www.cookfoodie.com/wishlist/san-sebastian

### Review

La Espiga feels like hanging out in the neighbor bar with friends and family, the service is fast, the Pintxos are really good. The wine selection is extensive, even by the glass. And they also have the claim to have started the pintxos in town. Get the Tortillita with truffles.

Opened in 1928. Luisa San Martín made the first banderillas here. The Castro family has run it for three generations. I was lucky to be introduced to some of the family through a friend, and they are just an amazing family. Three generations making pintxos and making sure that the quality is top-notch. Not only that, but the atmosphere is really good. If you notice the decoration, the floor resembles the same floor that you're gonna find in the streets of San Sebastian. There's wood on the roof of the bar that resembles a lot of trees from the Basque country, and the bar itself is made of the metal that you see in the harbor. And there's also the murals that you'll find in San Telmo Museum. So it really makes you continue being in San Sebastian while you're having some pintxos.

My recommendation is to always start with the cold ones, just look at what's available. The rollito de jamon is really good, and everything that has any sardine and their egg salads, but also ask for what they have in calientes. I have already told you about the tortillita with truffles, but they also do other tortillas, and they will also do pimentones fried, and croquetas. They also have an albondiga. And just amazing food. Everything is good. There's nothing where you're gonna miss out.

The terrace is good for friends, but I always recommend squeezing into the bar. And you can also reserve. They have a basement with fancier tables and dinner service if you wanna try their good stuff. Opening all week with a reduced menu Sundays and Mondays. And they also kinda are available until late, so pretty easy option from 10 AM till 10 PM every day of the week.

I went with friends and family, but definitely recommended for everyone. The price feels right. Of course, if you order a lot of tapas and you go to the restaurant, it might be a little bit on the upper end of pintxos, but still totally worth it.

My favorite place, it really felt like home, and I'm really glad that I was able to also understand who's behind it, how Chema and his brother run this place and keep it tight and amazing.

### What to order

- **Tortillita with trufa:** Soft tortilla with truffle; start here.
- **Rollito de jamón:** Cold pintxo of jamón rolled tight; grab it from the counter first.
- **Sardine pintxos:** Whatever sardine they have out that day; always worth it.
- **Egg salads:** Cold ensaladillas at the bar; easy with wine by the glass.
- **Pimentones fried:** Hot fried peppers when you move to calientes.
- **Croquetas:** Hot croquetas from the kitchen; ask what’s frying.
- **Albóndiga:** Their meatball; order it with the other calientes.

### Tips

Table reservations are by phone: +34 943 421 423. There is a basement with fancier tables and dinner service. I always recommend squeezing into the bar over the terrace.

### If you're visiting La Espiga

#### What should I order at La Espiga?

Start with the cold pintxos on the bar: the rollito de jamón, anything with sardine, and the egg salads. Then ask what they have in calientes: the Tortillita with truffles, other tortillas, fried pimentones, croquetas, and the albóndiga.

#### Do you need a reservation at La Espiga?

Not for the bar. I always recommend squeezing into the bar over the terrace. Table reservations are by phone at +34 943 421 423, including the basement with fancier tables and dinner service.

#### What are La Espiga's opening hours?

It opens every day of the week, from about 10 AM to 10 PM, with a reduced menu on Sundays and Mondays. Hours change, so check before you go.

#### Is La Espiga expensive?

The price feels right. If you order a lot, or eat in the restaurant downstairs, it lands on the upper end for pintxos in San Sebastián, but it is still worth it.

#### Where is La Espiga in San Sebastián?

San Martzial Kalea, 48, in the Centro of San Sebastián (Donostia), a short walk from the Parte Vieja.

## Sala de Despiece: I've been to three salas. I miss the original.

> Sala de Despiece review, Madrid: the giant tomato, the Rolex, raw chuletón, and fried artichoke at the bar. Wines by the glass.

- **Restaurant:** Sala de Despiece
- **City:** Madrid
- **Neighborhood:** Chamberí · Centro · Salamanca
- **Cuisine:** Contemporary Spanish
- **Rating:** 5/5
- **Must order:** Rolex
- **Address:** SDD1: Calle de Alonso Cano, 28, Madrid, Spain
- **Phone:** +34 919 590 603
- **Website:** https://www.saladedespiece.com/
- **Instagram:** https://www.instagram.com/saladedespiece/
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Sala+de+Despiece+SDD1+Calle+de+Alonso+Cano+28+Madrid
- **Reviewed:** 2026-09-26
- **Author:** Christian Van Der Henst (Cvander)
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/sala-de-despiece

### Review

I've been to three salas. I miss the original. The original Calle Ponzano (2013) closed in 2024; SDD1 moved to Alonso Cano. That is why I miss the original. They really appreciate Spanish produce, they have great wines, service is always very friendly. That gigantic tomato, the Rolex and the chuleta, just beautiful presented, assembled and it tastes amazing.

My friend zordor once told me about this place and ever since I religiously visited every time that I am in Madrid. This is not the typical place that you should be said if you wanna have a local experience in Spain, but I do believe that this is the kind of place that you should visit especially if you're a tourist and you wanna see a little bit of experimentation with great produce, amazing food, and good quality of customer service.

I once went to the original Sala that has been extended now to many new branches. I have been going to some of the newer ones and they basically have more room, but keep the same atmosphere. You will be sitting at a bar most of the time even if you come with a group and there will be someone helping you with drinks, great selection of wines by the glass and also bottles, and then you start asking for some of the plates. It's recommended to have a couple of plates per person or even more.

If you really wanna do some snacks from the menu I would always get the meat. It's raw and they call it chuletón and they make it into the wrap and it's just beautiful and the presentation and everything is amazing. And then never miss the Rolex. It has fuet and it's wrapped in bacon and also some truffles and an egg and it's basically a major explosion of flavors in your mouth. They do other amazing stuff like the artichoke, which is one of my favorite ones in Spain for the texture and how they fry it. Overall their food selection and everything that they would give you is amazing. It's part show to see part of the presentation of how they finish the dishes and it's always a great place. Great to bring your friends who are being introduced to Spanish cuisine or who already have an idea of how it works and wanna get something more experimental and upscale.

### What to order

- **Tomata:** Half-kilo tomato with brine, olive oil, and basil.
- **Rolex:** Fuet wrapped in bacon, truffle and egg. Finished at the counter.
- **Ribs:** Grilled ribs on the Sala paper.
- **Pulpo a la plancha:** Grilled octopus on the metal plate.
- **Alcachofa:** Fried artichoke petals; great texture.
- **Chuletón:** Raw beef wrap with tomato and tartufata.
- **Berenjena frita:** Fried aubergine with the fish and pink onions.

### Tips

Choose your sala when booking through the official website. The main map points to the current SDD1 address in Chamberí; all three current restaurants are listed below.

### Locations

- **SDD1 — Chamberí** (Chamberí, Madrid): Calle de Alonso Cano, 28, Madrid, Spain. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Sala+de+Despiece+SDD1+Calle+de+Alonso+Cano+28+Madrid. Current SDD1 in Chamberí. The original Calle Ponzano (2013) closed in 2024; SDD1 moved here to Alonso Cano. Reserve SDD1 on the official website.
- **SDD2 — Centro** (Centro, Madrid): Calle de la Virgen de los Peligros, 8, Madrid, Spain. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Sala+de+Despiece+SDD2+Calle+de+la+Virgen+de+los+Peligros+8+Madrid. The Centro restaurant, near Puerta del Sol. Choose SDD2 when reserving on the official website.
- **SDD0 — Salamanca** (Salamanca, Madrid): Calle de Ayala, 27, Madrid, Spain. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Sala+de+Despiece+SDD0+Calle+de+Ayala+27+Madrid. Also called Sala Zero. Choose SDD0 when reserving on the official website. Subcero, the group's cocktail and music space, is downstairs on level -1 at this same address, not a separate restaurant branch.

### If you're visiting Sala de Despiece

#### What should I order at Sala de Despiece?

Never miss the Rolex. Get the chuletón, the raw beef they make into a wrap, and the giant tomato. The fried artichoke is one of my favorites in Spain for its texture. Plan on a couple of plates per person or more.

#### Which Sala de Despiece should I go to?

There are three salas in Madrid: SDD1 in Chamberí (Calle de Alonso Cano, 28), SDD2 in Centro near Puerta del Sol (Calle de la Virgen de los Peligros, 8), and SDD0 in Salamanca (Calle de Ayala, 27). The original Calle Ponzano (2013) closed in 2024; SDD1 moved to Alonso Cano. I miss the original.

#### How do you book Sala de Despiece?

Book through the official website, saladedespiece.com, and choose your sala (SDD1, SDD2, or SDD0) when you reserve.

#### Is Sala de Despiece a traditional Spanish restaurant?

Not the typical local experience. It is great Spanish produce with some experimentation, friendly service, and part of the show is watching them finish the dishes at the counter. You sit at the bar most of the time, even with a group.

## La Cuchara de San Telmo: cochinillo, the skin is love. This is the best casual meal in San Sebastian.

> La Cuchara de San Telmo, San Sebastián: cochinillo skin, kokotxas, navajas. Tiny room, fast service, portions not cheap pintxos. Tue-Sun, closed Mon.

- **Restaurant:** La Cuchara de San Telmo
- **City:** San Sebastián
- **Neighborhood:** Parte Vieja
- **Cuisine:** Basque Pintxos
- **Rating:** 5/5
- **Must order:** Cochinillo
- **Ideal for:** Small groups
- **Address:** Santa Korda Kalea, 4, 20003 Donostia / San Sebastián, Spain
- **Phone:** +34 943 441 655
- **Instagram:** https://www.instagram.com/lacucharadesantelmo/
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=La+Cuchara+de+San+Telmo+Santa+Korda+Kalea+4+San+Sebastian
- **Reviewed:** 2026-09-06
- **Author:** Christian Van Der Henst (Cvander)
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/cuchara-de-san-telmo
- **City guide:** San Sebastián: https://www.cookfoodie.com/wishlist/san-sebastian

### Review

I've been to this place three times. And I will come back to this town to eat here. Cochinillo, the skin is love. The kokotxas. The Navajas. A good Txacolin.

Place gets crowded and it's only a few spots inside. Still worth it if you are a small group. Or wait for one of the 4 tables next to the place. You can even order some food and eat on the street if needed.

Service is fast, the food has stayed consistent over the years. First time here for me was in 2008. And they keep serving every meal with a lot of love.

In the pics, some of the tapas, except the Cochinillo and las Navajas, those are half portions, so you can safely try a lot of stuff to understand what they offer.

It's next to a museum, very small alley connects them. Since I'm coming back, this review is just getting started.

Also worth classic stops such as Ganbara and La Espiga while you are in San Sebastián.

### Guest perspective: A friend on La Cuchara de San Telmo

Another important review from somebody that joined me for the last visit:

> Siiii, esa piel de cerdo! Estaba buenisima!!!

> Crujiente!!!!

> Las navajas deliciosas! Mis respetos para el mesero! Rapidisimo y gentil, atendiendo todas las mesas all mismo tiempo!

### What to order

- **Kokotxas / Hake cheeks:** ES: Kokotxas confitadas y a la plancha. EN: Confit and grilled hake cheeks (kokotxas).
- **Navajas gallegas / Galician razor clams:** ES: Navajas gallegas abiertas con una mantequilla de vermut blanco. EN: Galician razor clams opened with white vermouth butter.
- **Bonito o merluza / Local tuna or hake:** ES: Bonito o merluza, asado con una vinagreta de pochas y refrito de vinagre de sidra. EN: Local tuna or hake, grilled with a white bean vinaigrette and cider-vinegar refrito.
- **Pulpo salteado / Sautéed Galician octopus:** ES: Pulpo salteado con pimentón de la Vera, aceite de oliva y tzatziki. EN: Galician octopus sautéed with La Vera paprika, olive oil and tzatziki.
- **Oreja de cerdo / Pressed and roasted pig's ear:** ES: Oreja de cerdo prensada y asada con sofrito de tomate y cebolla al tomillo limón. EN: Pressed and roasted pig's ear with tomato-and-onion sofrito and lemon thyme.
- **Cordero lechal / Roast suckling lamb:** ES: Cordero lechal asado en su jugo con hierbas provenzales, cremoso de apionabo y yogur. EN: Suckling lamb roasted in its own juices with Provençal herbs, creamy celeriac and yogurt sauce.
- **Cochinillo de Leitza / Slow-roasted Leitza piglet:** ES: Cochinillo de Leitza asado lentamente con cerveza a horno suave y membrillo Sta. Teresa de Jesús. EN: Leitza piglet slow-roasted with beer in a gentle oven, served with Sta. Teresa de Jesús quince paste.
- **Queso de cabra / Grilled goat cheese:** ES: Queso de cabra a la plancha relleno de piperrada, con vinagreta de mostaza y miel. EN: Grilled goat cheese filled with piperrada, with a mustard-and-honey vinaigrette.

### Tips

Crowded, only a few spots inside. Wait for one of the 4 tables next to the place, or eat on the street.

### If you're visiting La Cuchara de San Telmo

#### What are the hours at La Cuchara de San Telmo?

Tuesday to Sunday, lunch and dinner. Closed Monday. They do not have a website, so confirm before you go.

#### Is it worth waiting for a table, or should I eat inside?

Yes, wait. The room is tiny, only a few spots inside. Still worth it if you are a small group. Or wait for one of the 4 tables next to the place. You can even order some food and eat on the street if needed.

#### Is the service fast?

Yes. Service is fast, and the food has been consistent over the years.

#### Is it cheap tapas and pintxos?

No. They serve portions. Half portions on some plates, so you can still try a lot, but this is not the cheap counter-pintxo crawl.

## Arrosseria Antoni Rubies: Artesa de Lleida roadside Bib stop for arròs a la marinera

> Arrosseria Antoni Rubies, Artesa de Lleida: Bib Gourmand roadside stop for arròs a la marinera and cordero ribs.

- **Restaurant:** Arrosseria Antoni Rubies
- **City:** Artesa de Lleida / Lleida area
- **Neighborhood:** Artesa de Lleida
- **Cuisine:** Catalan / arroceria / rice
- **Rating:** 4/5
- **Price:** $$
- **Must order:** Arròs a la marinera
- **Ideal for:** A roadside rice stop near Lleida. Michelin Bib Gourmand.
- **Address:** Carrer de Lleida 6, 25150 Artesa de Lleida
- **Phone:** +34 973 167 553
- **Website:** https://antonirubies.com/
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Arrosseria+Antoni+Rubies+Carrer+de+Lleida+6+25150+Artesa+de+Lleida
- **Reviewed:** 2026-09-04
- **Author:** Cvander
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/arrosseria-antoni-rubies

### Review

At Arrosseria Antoni Rubies in Artesa de Lleida, stop for the rice. Order the arròs a la marinera for two, get the costillas de cordero, and leave room to look at the owner’s wall of old phones.

I was on my way to Lleida and started looking for restaurants. I wanted a small stop and a decent menú, the way they mean it in Spain. Finding this arroceria was a beautiful surprise. A small village outside Lleida, the place was full, and it carries a Michelin Bib Gourmand. We still got a table.

Near the table there is a collection of old smartphones. iPhones, iPods, some iPads, other phones, on display. The owner told me he has been collecting them since the early beginning of that technology.

What was on the menu for us was cordero. The ribs were fascinating. We also had an arroz. When you get a portion for two they bring a full paella, the big pan, with shrimp and all sorts of seafood including squid. It took a while to cook and it was really lovely. Service was really good. They have ice cream for dessert and other options, but we basically went for good paella, some ribs, and a little bread.

Very nice, cozy place. Definitely the stopover I was looking for. I would go back with a larger group and try all the different paellas, because that seems to be what they do better.

### What to order

- **Arròs a la marinera:** Plated portion with langoustine, mussels, shrimp. Order for two; they cook the rice.
- **Costillas de cordero:** Lamb ribs. What was on the menu for us was cordero.

### Tips

Full village room; we still got a table as a stopover. Worth the detour for rice.

### If you're visiting Arrosseria Antoni Rubies

#### What should I order at Arrosseria Antoni Rubies?

The arròs a la marinera for two, and the costillas de cordero (lamb). The rice takes a while and arrives as a plated portion with langoustine, mussels, shrimp.

#### Is Arrosseria Antoni Rubies in the Michelin Guide?

Yes. It carries a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

#### Where is Arrosseria Antoni Rubies?

Carrer de Lleida 6, 25150 Artesa de Lleida, a small village outside Lleida. It is a good roadside stop on the way to Lleida.

#### Can you get a table without booking at Antoni Rubies?

The village room was full when we stopped, and we still got a table as a stopover.

#### How long does the paella take at Antoni Rubies?

The rice for two takes a while to cook. It is worth the wait.

> Cervecería Catalana review, Barcelona: no reservations, fast service, great energy. Order the jamón, navajas, pincho de solomillo, and crema catalana.

- **Restaurant:** Cervecería Catalana
- **City:** Barcelona

### Review

Cervecería Catalana: still the happy place, walk in and wait.

A teacher pointed us here in a cool hunting class a few decades ago. Still today, any visit to Barcelona includes this room. Good for groups.

Mallorca 236. No reservations. You walk in, wait for a table, and the service is really efficient. The same team runs Ciudad Condal, Vinitus, and La Flauta. Same machine. Tapas is the specialty. The jamón was special this time.

Order the pincho de solomillo, pincho de gambas, navajas, and tortilla de patata. Pimientos de padrón, anchoas, and manchego. Local wine, or a caña. Clara or tinto de verano if you want to go light.

Finish always with crema catalana.

- **Anchoas**
- **Manchego**
- **Crema catalana**

### Tips

No reservations. Walk in and wait.

### If you're visiting Cervecería Catalana

#### Does Cervecería Catalana take reservations?

No. You walk in and wait for a table at Carrer de Mallorca 236. The service is really efficient, so the wait moves.

#### What should I order at Cervecería Catalana?

The jamón, pincho de solomillo, pincho de gambas, navajas, and tortilla de patata. Add pimientos de padrón, anchoas, and manchego, and always finish with crema catalana.

#### Is Cervecería Catalana good for groups?

Yes. It is good for groups, with great energy and fast service. The same team runs Ciudad Condal, Vinitus, and La Flauta.

#### What should I drink at Cervecería Catalana?

Local wine or a caña. Clara or tinto de verano if you want to go light.

## Geoboki Sikdang: Seoul pork BBQ where the skin is the point

> Geoboki Sikdang in Seoul serves charcoal-grilled pork, chewy kkeopdegi, grilled kimchi, and lunchtime soju near Kyung Hee University.

- **Restaurant:** Geoboki Sikdang (거복이식당)
- **City:** Seoul
- **Neighborhood:** Hoegi (Kyung Hee)
- **Cuisine:** Korean BBQ
- **Rating:** 4/5
- **Price:** $
- **Must order:** Pig skin (kkeopdegi) / pork skin
- **Ideal for:** A casual pork lunch with friends near Kyung Hee University
- **Address:** 6 Gyeonghee-daero 3-gil, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul (서울 동대문구 경희대로3길 6)
- **Phone:** 02-959-1559
- **Instagram:** https://www.instagram.com/geobokye_sikdang/
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Geoboki+Sikdang+%EA%B1%B0%EB%B3%B5%EC%9D%B4%EC%8B%9D%EB%8B%B9+%EA%B2%BD%ED%9D%AC%EB%8C%80%EB%A1%9C3%EA%B8%B8+6
- **Reviewed:** 2026-09-01
- **Author:** Cvander
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/geoboki-sikdang

### Review

At Geoboki Sikdang in Seoul, near Kyung Hee, come early for lunch. Order the pork, put kimchi on the charcoal, and leave room for the pork skin.

I really believe that Korean BBQ is amazing. I saw it in many K-dramas. I've enjoyed them in K-Town in LA and in Japantown in San Francisco. But also, I'm the biggest fan of San Ho Won (reviewed here already). So this trip to Seoul I wanted locals to show me their stuff. And this is what happened.

In California, going for Korean BBQ means mostly beef slices, a lot of wagyu and stuff they want to impress you with, bulgogi, etc. I got used to that because of K-Town in LA and the good options in the Bay Area. So when I asked friends in Seoul to impress me with Korean BBQ, I was happy to discover their passion for pork. No bulgogi, not sugar or weird marinated stuff.

This place opens early so it's easy to get a table before it gets crowded at night with the university students nearby. We were in a university area. A local friend and tour guide helped us with the cooking and helped us understand the culture. Seems like the traditions among students, and also between coworkers, have changed since Covid. Not only that, their pork selection is really good, and the pork skin is a different texture that I experienced firsthand here.

Pair it with some soju and beer. And make sure to also include some kimchi on the grill. Btw, the grill uses charcoal, and the management of both the fat with water and how clean it stays impressed me. Their marination doesn't abuse sugar like they do in America.

Good BBQ, good price, fun place to bring friends. Come early. Oh, the soju is cheaper than water if you have lunch here.

After your meal here, go for a walk. You’re walking distance to a beautiful park with the wall of the city, as well as brick buildings from major universities in Seoul. It’s really a beautiful walk and very necessary after the meal.

### Guest perspective: My partner on Geoboki Sikdang

My partner visited and really enjoyed the food. Her remarks:

> Pork belly was thick. Amazing that you don’t get any sugar or weird stuff in the marinade of the pork. The grill remained clean after the whole meal. You have to order the pork skin in advance.

### What to order

- **Big pork set (moksal + samgyeopsal):** Moksal and samgyeopsal over real charcoal. Order the set with as much pork as possible and try the different cuts.
- **Pork skin / kkeopdegi:** Chewy, scored pork skin with fat that gives. The texture is the point.
- **Kimchi on the grill:** Put the kimchi on the grill next to the pork skin. The heat changes the flavor.
- **Soju and beer:** Soju and beer with the pork. At lunch the soju is cheaper than water.

### Tips

Come for lunch before the student dinner rush.

### Locations

- **Hoegi / Kyung Hee (회기 본점)** (Hoegi / Kyung Hee, Seoul): 6 Gyeonghee-daero 3-gil, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Geoboki+Sikdang+%EA%B1%B0%EB%B3%B5%EC%9D%B4%EC%8B%9D%EB%8B%B9+%EA%B2%BD%ED%9D%AC%EB%8C%80%EB%A1%9C3%EA%B8%B8+6. The university-area room. This is the meal in this review. Come for lunch before the student dinner rush.
- **Daehangno / 대학로** (Daehangno, Seoul): 서울 종로구 동숭동 1-48. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Geoboki+Sikdang+%EA%B1%B0%EB%B3%B5%EC%9D%B4%EC%8B%9D%EB%8B%B9+%EC%84%9C%EC%9A%B8+%EC%A2%85%EB%A1%9C%EA%B5%AC+%EB%8F%99%EC%88%AD%EB%8F%99+1-48. Another Geoboki room in the family. Same pork energy, different neighborhood.

### If you're visiting Geoboki Sikdang

#### Why pork instead of beef?

California Korean BBQ is beef-heavy. In Seoul, friends who wanted to impress me went straight to pork. Locals are serious about it.

#### Which Geoboki Sikdang branch is this review about?

This review is from the Hoegi branch near Kyung Hee University. Geoboki has other rooms, including Daehangno, but this meal was Hoegi only.

#### What should I order at Geoboki Sikdang?

Order the big pork platter, pig skin, kimchi for the grill, and soju.

#### Should I visit for lunch or dinner?

Lunch is quiet. Dinner fills with university students, so come for lunch or arrive before the student dinner rush.

## 食令 SHABU at Taipei 101: live abalone, Iberico, and the crab they clean for you

> 食令 SHABU at Taipei 101: live abalone, Iberico in the soup, and crab they clean for you. 4F luxury floor, next to Dior.

- **Restaurant:** 食令 SHABU
- **City:** Taipei
- **Neighborhood:** Xinyi District
- **Cuisine:** Shabu-shabu
- **Rating:** 5/5
- **Price:** $$$$
- **Must order:** Live abalone
- **Ideal for:** A rainy day at Taipei 101
- **Address:** 4F, No. 45, Shifu Road, Xinyi District, Taipei 110
- **Phone:** +886-2-8101-7989
- **Website:** https://www.shilingshabu.com/
- **Instagram:** https://instagram.com/shi_ling_shabu_101
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=%E9%A3%9F%E4%BB%A4+SHABU+Taipei+101+No.+45+Shifu+Road
- **Reviewed:** 2026-08-29
- **Author:** Cvander
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/shi-ling-shabu
- **City guide:** Taipei: https://www.cookfoodie.com/wishlist/taipei

### Review

4F of Taipei 101, luxury floor, next to Dior. A few gourmet coffee shops with good desserts on that level too. In the corner by the elevator, this shabu. One trip with weeks near the tower and constant rain, we tried it.

Fresh is the word. Seafood plate: crab, jumbo shrimp, and the abalone still moving. Good beef. And to my surprise, cerdo ibérico. The Spanish pig famous for jamón, in the soup. People in Spain will judge me. Trust me, it was good.

Service is extraordinary. They help cook the seafood and clean the crab so you can eat. I asked for butter. Judgy look. Vinegar and ginger instead. New flavor for the collection.

Good shabu. The one I come back to next time. If you are here, go up to the observatory. The skyline keeps changing, and the damper that holds this place through earthquakes and storms is worth seeing.

### Guest perspective: Usagi on 食令 SHABU

Mi amiga Usagi estuvo en Taipei y esto es lo que pensó de Shabu:

> Me gustó este shabu mucho más que los de Japón. Todo se sentía más fresco, hasta orgánico. Que lleguen vivos los moluscos y el marisco le da un valor agregado, aunque sea un poco cruel. Te muestran los abalones moviéndose, los langostinos pidiendo ayuda, el cangrejo intentando huir. Luego se lo llevan y lo cortan. Yo no hubiera podido cortar el abalón entero. Demasiado cruel. Gracias por cortármelo.

> Fue la primera vez que vi jamón ibérico en un shabu. En Japón no hay eso. Probamos el ibérico hervido. Un crimen en España, pero estaba rico, no me quejo.

> En Japón el shabu lo haces tú. Acá metían todo, sacaban todo y te lo dejaban listo. Más relax. Por eso se sintió más high-class.

> Recomiendo mucho el menú surf and turf: carne y mar. Éramos tres y con eso y el ibérico me llené. Calidad. Nunca había comido tomate en un shabu. Me sorprendió el postre: pudín, sandía, helado de matcha. En Japón, en un menú así, casi no viene.

> No sentí necesidad de pedir más verduras ni más carne. Súper recomendado. Imagino que no fue barato. Por la experiencia, vale la pena.

### What to order

- **Live abalone:** Still moving on the seafood plate. Fresh is the word.
- **Crab:** They help cook the seafood and clean the crab so you can eat.
- **Jumbo shrimp:** Part of the seafood plate with the crab and live abalone.
- **Cerdo ibérico:** The Spanish pig famous for jamón, in the soup. People in Spain will judge me. Trust me, it was good.
- **Beef:** Good beef in the shabu.

### Tips

4F luxury floor of Taipei 101, next to Dior, in the corner by the elevator.

### If you're visiting 食令 SHABU

#### Where is 食令 SHABU in Taipei 101?

4F of Taipei 101, luxury floor, next to Dior. In the corner by the elevator. A few gourmet coffee shops with good desserts on that level too.

#### What should I order at 食令 SHABU?

Seafood plate: crab, jumbo shrimp, and the abalone still moving. Good beef. And to my surprise, cerdo ibérico. They help cook the seafood and clean the crab so you can eat.

#### Do they serve crab with butter?

I asked for butter. Judgy look. Vinegar and ginger instead. New flavor for the collection.

#### Should I go to the Taipei 101 observatory after?

If you are here, go up to the observatory. The skyline keeps changing, and the damper that holds this place through earthquakes and storms is worth seeing.

## A love letter to Din Tai Fung

> A love letter to Din Tai Fung: xiaolongbao, chilled cucumber salad, and the original Xinyi Road shop in Taipei, plus favorite branches worldwide.

- **Restaurant:** Din Tai Fung
- **City:** Taipei
- **Neighborhood:** Da'an District
- **Cuisine:** Taiwanese
- **Rating:** 5/5
- **Price:** $$
- **Must order:** Xiaolongbao
- **Ideal for:** Groups, travelers, and anyone who wants a taste of Taiwan
- **Address:** No. 194, Section 2, Xinyi Road, Da'an District, Taipei 106
- **Phone:** +886-2-2321-8928
- **Website:** https://www.dintaifung.com.tw/eng/
- **Instagram:** https://instagram.com/dintaifung.tw
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Din+Tai+Fung+No.+194+Section+2+Xinyi+Road+Taipei
- **Reviewed:** 2026-08-28
- **Author:** Christian Van Der Henst (Cvander)
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/din-tai-fung
- **City guide:** Taipei: https://www.cookfoodie.com/wishlist/taipei

### Review

This is more than a review. It is a love letter to one of my favorite restaurants in the world.

I first tried Din Tai Fung in Hong Kong. In Kowloon I remember a branch with a Michelin star: one of those starred restaurants you actually had to try because it was affordable. I had no idea that this chain, and Taiwan itself, would become such a fun tradition in my life.

Din Tai Fung, or DTF: Down to Foodie. For me, it has become one of the flavors of Taiwan. Anyone who visits the island learns that locals really push this place. Friends in Taipei keep inviting me, and I usually let them order so I can learn what they love.

If you want the fancy location, there are a few in Xinyi. Taipei 101 (mall and observatory are mandatory) is busy. There is another one close by at A4. I dare you to try the original Xinyi Road shop in Da'an. That original is now takeaway-only. For dine-in, the Xinsheng flagship is across the street.

If you are elsewhere in the world, go to one of the big ones. The Las Vegas branch is one of my favorites: inside ARIA, on the casino floor, windows looking toward Vdara and Nancy Rubins' Big Edge, that large cactus-like sculpture. That view is part of what makes it fun. Westfield Valley Fair is the Bay Area mall branch, and where I occasionally end up for brunch. Los Angeles has many; Century City is one in a big mall, close after landing at LAX. There is still no San Francisco branch, which is fortunate: it stays something I look forward to when I travel.

In October 2026 I went to the Santa Monica Place branch. The Taiwanese cabbage was a very interesting surprise. Highly recommend it, and the wood ear mushrooms; they complement anything you order. For something different, get the kimchi and pork dumplings, unlike anything I've tried at other Din Tai Fungs.

In Taiwan I always go to Din Tai Fung. Get the xiaolongbao, the chilled cucumber salad with chili oil, and the soups. The hot-and-sour soup is amazing, and the chicken soup is really well done. Pot stickers are a must. Far from Taiwan, their boba tea is also good; in Taiwan, try other boba shops. Have the specialties at the restaurant, including the dessert xiaolongbao. They experiment with flavors and local stuff at many branches. It is always worth it.

Din Tai Fung is Taiwan. We should all try the flavors of this country. It has become a huge American business, but it still earns that loyalty. Worth it, and affordable for groups.

### Guest perspective: A friend on Din Tai Fung

A friend has been to Din Tai Fung about fifty times. Her take:

> The xiaolongbao skin is very thin and the broth is rich and juicy. A million branches from this chain and the quality is still there. They understand consistency.

> Hot and sour soup is in the favorites. And don’t forget to order the dessert baos. They know how to do desserts.

### What to order

- **Xiaolongbao:** The soup dumplings that made the chain famous. Eighteen pleats, thin skin, hot broth. Always start here, including the dessert versions.
- **Chilled Cucumber Salad with Chili Oil:** Cold, crunchy cucumbers in chili oil. The first thing I order every time I sit down.
- **Hot-and-Sour Soup:** Bright, spicy, and one of the soups that makes me keep coming back.
- **Chicken Soup:** Clean, well-made chicken soup. Simple, and really well done.
- **Pot Stickers:** Crispy-bottom dumplings. A must.
- **Dessert Xiaolongbao:** Sweet soup dumplings and other dessert specials. They experiment with flavors and local stuff in many branches.
- **Boba Tea:** If you are far from Taiwan, their boba tea is also good. In Taiwan, I would recommend trying other boba shops.
- **Taiwanese Cabbage with Garlic:** A very interesting surprise at Santa Monica Place. Highly recommend it; it complements anything you order.
- **Wood Ear Mushrooms in a Vinegar Dressing:** Had them at Santa Monica Place. Highly recommend; they complement anything you order.
- **Kimchi & Kurobuta Pork Dumplings:** For something different. Unlike anything I've tried at other Din Tai Fungs. Had them at Santa Monica Place.

### Tips

Walk in. The original Xinyi Road shop is takeaway-only now; for dine-in, use the Xinsheng flagship across the street, Taipei 101, A4, or one of the big locations abroad.

### Locations

- **Original Xinyi Road** (Da'an District, Taipei): No. 194, Section 2, Xinyi Road, Da'an District, Taipei 106. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Din+Tai+Fung+No.+194+Section+2+Xinyi+Road+Taipei. The original storefront in Da'an. Now takeaway-only. For dine-in, the Xinsheng flagship is across the street.
- **Taipei 101** (Xinyi District, Taipei): B1, No. 45, Shifu Road, Xinyi District, Taipei 110. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Din+Tai+Fung+Taipei+101+No.+45+Shifu+Road. The mall and the observatory are mandatory. This branch is busy.
- **Xinyi A4** (Xinyi District, Taipei): B2, No. 19, Songgao Road, Xinyi District, Taipei 110. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Din+Tai+Fung+Shin+Kong+Mitsukoshi+A4+Songgao+Road+Taipei. Another Xinyi branch, close to Taipei 101, in Shin Kong Mitsukoshi A4.
- **Hong Kong, Kowloon** (Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong): Shop 306, 3/F, Silvercord, 30 Canton Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Din+Tai+Fung+Silvercord+30+Canton+Road+Tsim+Sha+Tsui+Kowloon. In Kowloon I remember visiting one with the Michelin star award.
- **ARIA Resort & Casino** (Las Vegas Strip, Las Vegas): 3730 S Las Vegas Blvd, Las Vegas, NV 89158. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Din+Tai+Fung+ARIA+3730+S+Las+Vegas+Blvd. The restaurant's windows look toward Vdara and Nancy Rubins' Big Edge installation, the large cactus-like structure.
- **Westfield Valley Fair** (Santa Clara / San Jose, Santa Clara): 2855 Stevens Creek Blvd, #1259, Santa Clara, CA 95050. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Din+Tai+Fung+Westfield+Valley+Fair+Santa+Clara. This is the mall branch for the Bay Area, and where I occasionally end up for brunch.
- **Century City** (Century City, Los Angeles): 10250 Santa Monica Blvd, #2400, Los Angeles, CA 90067. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Din+Tai+Fung+Westfield+Century+City+10250+Santa+Monica+Blvd. A new one in a big mall. Los Angeles has many options, but this is always close after landing in LAX.
- **Santa Monica Place** (Santa Monica Place, Santa Monica): 395 Santa Monica Pl, Level 3, Santa Monica, CA 90401. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Din+Tai+Fung+Santa+Monica+Place+395+Santa+Monica+Pl. Outdoor patio space, great on a nice day. Very close to the Santa Monica Pier, easy parking. Visited Oct 2026.

### If you're visiting Din Tai Fung

#### Which Din Tai Fung should I visit in Taipei?

The Taipei 101 mall and the observatory are mandatory, and that branch is busy. There is also another one close at A4, in Shin Kong Mitsukoshi. The original Xinyi Road shop in Da'an is now takeaway-only; for dine-in, the Xinsheng flagship is across the street.

#### Is Din Tai Fung only a Taipei restaurant?

No. It is a chain, and that is part of the fun. I first tried it in Kowloon, Hong Kong, at a Michelin-starred location. I keep going back in Taipei, and I have favorites at ARIA in Las Vegas and Westfield Valley Fair in Santa Clara. Los Angeles has many, including Century City after landing at LAX. There is still no San Francisco branch, so it remains something I look forward to when I travel.

#### What should I order at Din Tai Fung?

Xiaolongbao first, then the chilled cucumber salad with chili oil. Get the hot-and-sour soup and the chicken soup. Pot stickers are a must. It is worth having the specialties at the restaurant, including the dessert xiaolongbao. Far from Taiwan, their boba tea is also good; in Taiwan, try other boba shops.

#### Is Din Tai Fung expensive?

It is one of those Michelin-starred restaurants that you had to try because it was affordable. In Taiwan it is still a great value. It has become a huge American business, but it still earns the loyalty, especially for groups.

## El Chato is that Spanish corner that brings vibes of Madrid to the Mission.

> El Chato is that Spanish corner that brings Madrid to the Mission. Tortilla española, navajas, jamón, chatos of natural wine, and vermut.

- **Restaurant:** El Chato
- **City:** San Francisco
- **Neighborhood:** Mission
- **Cuisine:** Spanish Tapas
- **Rating:** 4/5
- **Price:** $$
- **Must order:** Tortilla Española
- **Ideal for:** Long afternoons, tapas grazing, and following Spain
- **Address:** 2301 Bryant St, San Francisco, CA 94110
- **Instagram:** https://instagram.com/elchatosf
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps?q=El+Chato+San+Francisco+Mission
- **Reviewed:** 2026-07-14
- **Author:** Christian Van Der Henst (Cvander)
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/el-chato
- **City guide:** San Francisco: https://www.cookfoodie.com/wishlist/san-francisco

### Review

This corner really makes Madrid a thing in the Mission. Beautiful place, great owners, and the kind of bar you end up trusting with a whole afternoon.

Spending a lot of time in Madrid, Barcelona, Granada and San Sebastián, you develop a love for the passion of Spanish food. And finding that same character in their owners, that love for making a tortilla taste good and caring for the bread and the vermuts, that's what makes El Chato a place where you feel in España.

It's a natural wine bar. Go for the tapas, the tortilla española, and the wines. They're just amazing. I really enjoy the navajas, and their jamón and cheese selection. Ask for some chatos so you can try more of what they have on the menu. The owners' passion shows in the food and in a list that leans on small European producers. The tortilla is simple, soft inside and golden at the edges.

They serve that tortilla as a pintxo on grilled bread with piquillo and allioli. Get pan con tomate with it, and spread the tomato yourself. The toasted jamón sandwich with melted cheese and piparras is the other plate I keep in the middle of the table.

During the World Cup this was a great community for following Spain. Locals and Spaniards hanging out, sharing an Estrella, calling the goals, passing around tortilla de patata and their vermut. They have a great non-alcoholic one for those early matches. The team is friendly. Trust their recommendations from the wine stand.

On a sunny day (the Mission gets better weather than the rest of the city) you can hang out outside. That corner doesn't just feel Mission. A friend said it could be Roma in Mexico City, Castellana in Madrid, Palermo Soho in Buenos Aires, or Providencia in Chile. There's a vibe in the corner.

Feels like a slice of Madrid in the Mission, with warm hospitality and flavors that actually hold up.

### What to order

- **Tortilla Española:** The simple, deep version you want: custardy inside, golden at the edges. They serve it as a pintxo on grilled bread with piquillo and allioli. During the World Cup it kept getting passed around with vermut and Estrella.
- **Navajas:** Galician razor clams from the conservas list. One of the dishes I keep coming back for.
- **Jamón and Cheese:** A proper Spanish jamón and cheese selection. Get the toasted jamón sandwich too: melted cheese, piparras, paprika, chips on the side.
- **Pan con Tomate:** Toasted bread with olive oil and grated tomato you spread yourself. The simple Spanish bite that belongs next to the tortilla and a chato of wine.
- **Chatos of Natural Wine:** Ask for chatos: small glasses so you can try more of the list. It leans on small European producers. Trust their recommendations from the wine stand.
- **Vermut:** Their vermut is part of the afternoon. They also have a great non-alcoholic one for those early World Cup matches.
- **Estrella Galicia:** The beer that shows up when Spain is playing. Share one with the table while you call the goals.

### Tips

Small corner bar. Walk in, grab an outside table on a sunny Mission day, or trust the team at the wine stand.

### If you're visiting El Chato

#### What are 'chatos' at El Chato?

Chatos are small glasses of wine, a traditional way to taste and explore in Spanish bars. Ask for some so you can try more of the natural wine list, which leans on small European producers. Trust the recommendations from the wine stand.

#### What should I order at El Chato?

Go for the tapas, the tortilla española, and the wines. The tortilla is custardy inside and golden at the edges, served as a pintxo. I really enjoy the navajas, the jamón and cheese, and pan con tomate. Ask for chatos. Get vermut, including the non-alcoholic one if you are there early, or share an Estrella.

#### Does El Chato have non-alcoholic drinks?

Yes. They have a great non-alcoholic vermut, which is what you want for those early World Cup matches.

#### Is there outdoor seating at El Chato?

Yes. On a sunny day you can hang out outside on the corner of Bryant and 21st. The Mission gets better weather than the rest of the city, and that sidewalk is part of the vibe.

#### Is El Chato a restaurant or a bar?

El Chato is a natural wine bar that serves excellent tapas. It is the kind of bar you end up trusting with a whole afternoon: come for the wine, stay for the tortilla española, and let the corner do the rest.

## Nasi lemak at The Coconut Club Beach Road, next to Arab Street

> Nasi lemak at The Coconut Club Beach Road near Arab Street and Masjid Sultan, with ayam goreng berempah, beef rendang, and homemade otah.

- **Restaurant:** The Coconut Club Beach Road
- **City:** Singapore
- **Neighborhood:** Beach Road / Kampong Gelam
- **Cuisine:** Singaporean / Malay
- **Rating:** 4/5
- **Price:** $$
- **Must order:** Ayam Goreng Berempah
- **Ideal for:** Nasi lemak with friends in Kampong Gelam
- **Address:** 269 Beach Road, Singapore 199546
- **Phone:** +65 8725 3315
- **Website:** https://www.thecoconutclub.sg/beach-road
- **Instagram:** https://www.instagram.com/thecoconutclubsg/
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=The+Coconut+Club+Beach+Road+269+Beach+Road+Singapore+199546
- **Reviewed:** 2025-07-01
- **Author:** Cvander
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/the-coconut-club-beach-road

### Review

At The Coconut Club on Beach Road in Singapore, come for the nasi lemak. Order the ayam goreng berempah, get the beef rendang too, and don't skip the otah on the banana leaf.

A good friend invited me to try some of the local cuisine. I had some variation of this eating at another friend's house and also at a hawker market, but having the opportunity to explore a more interesting version of it in a beautiful setting is what attracted me to this place. And yes, the portions are big. The food is strong. I would say that after these we had to go for a walk and also a beautiful massage nearby. So yeah, this was really good food.

The Singaporean flavors were there. I really enjoyed seeing how they cook some of this on leaves, reminding me of some of the Latin cuisine. Egg fried stuff, and of course the rice to love.

It's also fascinating the location of the restaurant. It's close to Arab Street and Masjid Sultan, so you get to experience the variety and different approaches that Singapore has to offer. Great location, very nice atmosphere. Service was quick and the food came up very fast. I kind of feel like I got a kiss from Singapore with this beautiful meal.

### What to order

- **Ayam Goreng Berempah Leg Set:** Nasi lemak with spiced fried organic poulet leg.
- **Beef Rendang nasi lemak set:** Beef rendang served as a nasi lemak set.
- **Homemade Otah:** Charcoal-grilled on a banana leaf.

### Tips

Book via thecoconutclub.sg; communal tables

### If you're visiting The Coconut Club Beach Road

#### What should I order at The Coconut Club?

Come for the nasi lemak. Order the ayam goreng berempah, get the beef rendang too, and don't skip the homemade otah, charcoal-grilled on a banana leaf.

#### Do you need a reservation at The Coconut Club Beach Road?

Book through thecoconutclub.sg. Seating is at communal tables, and the food comes out fast.

#### Where is The Coconut Club Beach Road?

269 Beach Road, Singapore 199546, in Kampong Gelam, close to Arab Street and Masjid Sultan.

#### Are the portions big at The Coconut Club?

Yes. The portions are big and the food is strong. After our meal we went for a walk.

## Mijoté: The sushi bar where you get a French omakase in the Mission

> Mijoté review, San Francisco: former Mission sushi bar, weekly four-course French prix fixe. Sit at the bar, love the bread, ask what wine is on today.

- **Restaurant:** Mijoté
- **City:** San Francisco
- **Neighborhood:** Mission
- **Cuisine:** French
- **Rating:** 5/5
- **Price:** $$$
- **Must order:** Weekly four-course prix fixe
- **Ideal for:** Intimate dinners and food enthusiasts
- **Address:** 2400 Harrison St, San Francisco, CA 94110
- **Website:** https://www.mijotesf.com
- **Instagram:** https://instagram.com/mijotesf
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps?q=Mijoté+San+Francisco+Mission
- **Reservations:** https://resy.com/cities/sf/mijote
- **Reviewed:** 2025-01-27
- **Author:** Christian Van Der Henst (Cvander)
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/mijote
- **City guide:** San Francisco: https://www.cookfoodie.com/wishlist/san-francisco

### Review

I didn't really understand why I liked this restaurant so much the first time I was there, but it was probably because I was sitting at the bar next to the chef and he was finishing all these delicious French plates in front of me. And then it hit me. This used to be a sushi bar, and they kept that dynamic. They bring all the experience of cooking French food in Paris into San Francisco, but they do it and serve the plates with all the finishing touches right in front of you. That's kind of nice. Mijoté has a great, minimalistic, fixed-price menu with a couple of add-ons. You're going to love their bread and check the pairings or just see what's eclectic today in their wine list because they always have some great stuff. And make sure to ask to be seated at the bar. That's the best location.

### Guest perspective: My partner on Mijoté

My partner chose Mijoté. Her take:

> Mijoté is an affordable tasting in San Francisco. Incredible that the chef turned a sushi bar into a fresh experience. Chef from Japan worked in a famous bistro in Paris. We’re so lucky to have him in San Francisco.

> The menu and service are unpretentious and you get very good French food.

### What to order

- **Weekly four-course prix fixe:** Fixed-price French menu that changes weekly, with a couple of add-ons. Sit at the bar.
- **Lamb loin with saffron:** From a weekly menu card.
- **Bread:** You are going to love their bread.
- **Wine list:** Check the pairings or whatever is eclectic on the wine list that day.

### Tips

Request bar seating for the best experience watching the chefs

### If you're visiting Mijoté

#### Where should I sit at Mijoté?

Ask to be seated at the bar. That is the best location. You watch the chef finish the French plates right in front of you.

#### What is the menu like at Mijoté?

Weekly four-course prix fixe with a couple of add-ons. You are going to love their bread. Check the pairings or whatever is eclectic on the wine list that day.

#### Why does Mijoté feel different?

This used to be a sushi bar and they kept that dynamic. French cooking with the finishing touches right in front of you. That is kind of nice.

## Mosto: The mezcal bar of the Mission where you can have good pastor tacos.

> Tacolicious has a small mezcal bar next door in the Mission: Mosto. Pastor tacos from a proper trompo, and the pastor that the Mission gives.

- **Restaurant:** Mosto
- **City:** San Francisco
- **Neighborhood:** Mission
- **Cuisine:** Mexican
- **Rating:** 4/5
- **Price:** $$
- **Must order:** Tacos Al Pastor
- **Ideal for:** Late-night tacos and mezcal with friends
- **Address:** 741A Valencia St, San Francisco, CA 94110

- **City guide:** San Francisco: https://www.cookfoodie.com/wishlist/san-francisco

### Review

We have a real mezcal bar in San Francisco. Is the sister little property of Tacolicious. Mosto/El Burger also has good pastor. Skip the burgers.

There's a picture of Obama, and that guy knew about good food when I saw him on a little banquito in Hanoi eating bún chả with Bourdain, so I will trust his selection of tacos. Not sure if he paired them with some mezcal.

The tacos al pastor come from a proper trompo and remain the reason to go. Carved with char, pineapple, and salsa. We did a small reel when we visited. Check it out. They have a good mezcal selection too. Lately they are also making burgers, but I think that loses part of what made me recommend them the first time. Stick to the pastor. Skip the burgers.

### What to order

- **Tacos Al Pastor:** Carved from a proper trompo with char, pineapple, and salsa.

### Tips

Walk-ins welcome; busiest after 10pm on weekends

### If you're visiting Mosto

#### Is Mosto the bar next to Tacolicious?

Tacolicious has a small bar next door. Might be the extra space but for me, it has always been the main attraction. A full mezcal bar, with pastor tacos. Intimate. With banda linda. The pastor that the Mission gives.

#### What should I order at Mosto?

Stick to the pastor. It comes from a proper trompo, carved with char, pineapple, and salsa. Skip the burgers. That loses part of what made me recommend them.

#### Do they have mezcal?

Yes. Good mezcal selection. That is half the point.

## Burma Love: the Valencia branch is the best one, get the tea leaf salad.

> Burma Love review, San Francisco: the Valencia branch is the best one. Get the tea leaf salad, coconut rice, a curry, and noodle soup at the round table.

- **Restaurant:** Burma Love
- **City:** San Francisco
- **Neighborhood:** Mission
- **Cuisine:** Burmese
- **Rating:** 4/5
- **Price:** $$
- **Must order:** Tea Leaf Salad
- **Ideal for:** Groups at the round table, and anyone discovering Burmese food
- **Address:** 211 Valencia St, San Francisco, CA 94103
- **Phone:** +1-415-861-2100
- **Website:** https://www.burmalove.com
- **Instagram:** https://instagram.com/burmalovesf
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps?q=Burma+Love+San+Francisco+Valencia
- **Reviewed:** 2025-01-27
- **Author:** Christian Van Der Henst (Cvander)
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/burma-love
- **City guide:** San Francisco: https://www.cookfoodie.com/wishlist/san-francisco

### Review

The Valencia branch is the best one. Find an excuse to reserve the big round table: bring a group so you can try it all. Get there early for a drink at the bar.

You have to try the tea leaf salad because those fermented tea leaves are amazing and it has a great umami magic. Also, the coconut rice is great and I always include at least a curry, a soup with noodles, and some chicken.

Menlo Park and Mint Plaza get special mention. Same family, same tea leaf salad, a different room: Springline on the Peninsula, and the downtown dining room on Mint Plaza.

Now there are sister properties too. Kayah by Burma Love is at Thrive City next to Chase Center, the one you want before a Warriors game. Teakwood by Burma Love is the Hayes Valley room, more of a fire-warmed, special-occasion table.

This place introduced Burmese cuisine to many Americans, and Valencia is still the one I trust with a whole afternoon.

### What to order

- **Tea Leaf Salad:** Fermented tea leaves with nuts, seeds, and fresh vegetables. Great umami magic.
- **Coconut Rice:** I always include the coconut rice.
- **Curry:** I always include at least a curry.
- **Noodle soup:** A soup with noodles.
- **Chicken:** And some chicken.

### Tips

At Valencia, find an excuse to reserve the big round table. Get there early for a drink at the bar.

### Locations

- **Valencia** (Mission, San Francisco): 211 Valencia St, San Francisco, CA 94103. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Burma+Love+211+Valencia+Street+San+Francisco. The best branch. Reserve the big round table and get there early for a drink at the bar.
- **Mint Plaza** (Downtown, San Francisco): 8 Mint Plaza, San Francisco, CA 94103. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Burma+Love+8+Mint+Plaza+San+Francisco. Special mention. Same family, same tea leaf salad, a bigger downtown room.
- **Menlo Park** (Springline, Menlo Park): 1302 El Camino Real, Menlo Park, CA 94025. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Burma+Love+1302+El+Camino+Real+Menlo+Park. Special mention. The Peninsula table, at Springline.
- **Kayah by Burma Love** (Chase Center / Thrive City, San Francisco): 151 Warriors Way, San Francisco, CA 94158. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Kayah+by+Burma+Love+151+Warriors+Way+San+Francisco. Sister property at Thrive City next to Chase Center. The one before a Warriors game.
- **Teakwood by Burma Love** (Hayes Valley, San Francisco): 399 Grove St, San Francisco, CA 94102. Map: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Teakwood+by+Burma+Love+399+Grove+Street+San+Francisco. Sister property in Hayes Valley. The fire-warmed, special-occasion room.

### If you're visiting Burma Love

#### What is special about Burmese tea leaf salad?

You have to try it. Those fermented tea leaves are amazing and it has a great umami magic.

#### Which Burma Love location is best?

The Valencia branch in the Mission is the best one. Find an excuse to reserve the big round table, and get there early for a drink at the bar. Menlo Park and Mint Plaza get special mention. The sister properties are Kayah and Teakwood.

#### How should I book Burma Love on Valencia?

Reserve the big round table so a group can share tea leaf salad, coconut rice, a curry, a noodle soup, and some chicken. Get there early and have a drink at the bar before you sit.

## La Taqueria: This is my top burrito in San Francisco. Tacos are also great.

> La Taqueria review: my top burrito in San Francisco's Mission. Carne asada, supreme, no rice, extra guac. The Michelin line is long; come back for tacos.

- **Restaurant:** La Taqueria
- **City:** San Francisco
- **Neighborhood:** Mission
- **Cuisine:** Mexican
- **Rating:** 5/5
- **Price:** $
- **Must order:** Carne Asada Burrito (Supreme)
- **Ideal for:** Anyone seeking SF's best burrito, then tacos on the next visit
- **Address:** 2889 Mission St, San Francisco, CA 94110
- **Phone:** +1-415-285-7117
- **Instagram:** https://instagram.com/lataqueriasf
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps?q=La+Taqueria+San+Francisco+Mission
- **Reviewed:** 2025-01-27
- **Author:** Cvander and Aldo
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/la-taqueria
- **City guide:** San Francisco: https://www.cookfoodie.com/wishlist/san-francisco

### Review

This is my top burrito in San Francisco. Since appearing in the Michelin guide, the line got really big. Still worth it. No rice, pure love of carne asada. Funny that you get a burrito at La Taqueria. Go for the carne asada, make it supreme, ask for extra guac if you want. The carne asada is grilled to order.

If you are repeating, make sure to try the variety of tacos. The salsa is amazing. They even have issues with people stealing the containers. Part of the Mission's taqueria culture for decades, La Taqueria has been doing this long enough that the name is a little joke on first-timers: you come for the burrito, then you come back for the tacos.

We are still missing a proper burrito photo. For now, at least we have the carne asada on the grill and the actual tacos on the table.

### Guest perspective: Aldo on La Taqueria

Se ha vuelto una tradición ir por La Taquería con mi amigo Aldo. Su opinión:

> Lo más cercano a un burrito sonorense en EEUU con salsa que SÍ pica.

### What to order

- **Carne Asada Burrito (Supreme):** Grilled-to-order steak burrito with sour cream, guac, and cheese -no rice
- **Extra Guacamole:** Fresh, chunky guacamole made daily
- **Carne Asada Tacos:** Simple, perfect tacos with tender grilled beef and fresh salsa

### Tips

No reservations. The Michelin-guide line is long; go at off-peak hours.

### If you're visiting La Taqueria

#### What makes La Taqueria's burrito special?

This is my top burrito in San Francisco. No rice, pure love of carne asada. Funny that you get a burrito at a place called La Taqueria, but the carne asada is grilled to order and that is the whole point.

#### Why is the line so long?

Since appearing in the Michelin guide, the line got really big. It is still worth it. Go at off-peak hours if you can, but the wait is part of getting the best burrito in the city.

#### Should I get tacos or a burrito?

Get the burrito first. If you are repeating, make sure to try the variety of tacos. The salsa is amazing. They even have issues with people stealing the containers.

## Casa Escobar, where I go to get some Guatemalan lomito

> Casa Escobar Cayalá, Guatemala City: get the Mar y Tierra, lomito with giant shrimps, and ask for the local lomito and chorizo. Great steak, fast service.

- **Restaurant:** Casa Escobar
- **City:** Guatemala City
- **Neighborhood:** Cayalá
- **Cuisine:** Steakhouse
- **Rating:** 4/5
- **Must order:** Mar y Tierra
- **Ideal for:** Friends and family
- **Address:** Paseo Cayalá, Edificio GT local 107, Guatemala City
- **Phone:** +502 2354-4800
- **Website:** https://casaescobar.com.gt/
- **Instagram:** https://www.instagram.com/casaescobargt/
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=14.610064,-90.486264
- **Reviewed:** 2025-01-13
- **Author:** Cvander
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/casa-escobar

### Review

At Casa Escobar in Guatemala City, get the Mar y Tierra: lomito with giant shrimps.

Casa Escobar in the Cayalá city sits in the main area of the mall. Great location, where people like to hang out and eat. Great steak. They push international ingredients and methods: the puyazo (picanha) is from the US. Lomito comes both ways, US or local: ask for the local. It's really good. So is the local chorizo. They also do Argentinian chorizo made here following an Argentine recipe. Good wines from Argentina and Chile with the meat. Fast service, courses well timed, and they treat you properly. Fun with friends and family. Last visit was a big parrillada: carne adobada (pork), a bit dry but a different flavor, even if similar to Mexico. Also chicken, and tortillitas calientes. Consistent quality asado, carne asada the Guatemalan way. I recommend it.

Antigua was recently remodeled. Looks amazing. Nice service. One block from the parque central. Went back October 4, 2026 with friends. The Antigua location shines with the views to the ruins of La Compañía de Jesús. Good walk afterwards to the Spanish building, the Centro de Formación de la Cooperación Española, to check an exhibit.

Zona 10 / Guatemala City is more executive. Business during the week, families on weekends.

### What to order

- **Mar y Tierra:** Lomito with giant shrimps. The one to get.
- **Local lomito:** Ask for the local cut. Really good.
- **Tortillas Chancol:** Tortillitas calientes with cheese. Get them.
- **Local chorizo:** Really good. They also do Argentinian chorizo made here following an Argentine recipe.

### Tips

Cayalá: Paseo Cayalá, Edificio GT local 107. Antigua: one block from the parque central. Also Zona 10.

### If you're visiting Casa Escobar

#### Where is Casa Escobar in Cayalá?

Paseo Cayalá, Edificio GT local 107, in the main area of the mall.

#### What should I order at Casa Escobar?

The Mar y Tierra: lomito with giant shrimps. Ask for the local lomito and the local chorizo, both really good. And get the Tortillas Chancol, tortillitas calientes with cheese.

#### Should I order the imported or the local cuts?

Puyazo (picanha) is imported from the US. Lomito comes both ways, US or local: ask for the local, it's really good. Local chorizo is really good too, and they also do Argentinian chorizo made here following an Argentine recipe.

#### Antigua or Zona 10?

Antigua was recently remodeled. Looks amazing, nice service, one block from the parque central. Zona 10 is more executive: business during the week, families on weekends.

## Le Palais: book the duck, 先知鴨 or 火焰片皮鴨

> Le Palais review, Taipei: three-Michelin-star Cantonese duck at Palais de Chine. Pre-order 先知鴨 or 火焰片皮鴨 when you book.

- **Restaurant:** Le Palais
- **City:** Taipei
- **Neighborhood:** Datong
- **Cuisine:** Cantonese
- **Rating:** 5/5
- **Price:** $$$$
- **Must order:** 先知鴨 or 火焰片皮鴨
- **Ideal for:** Celebrations / friends visiting Taipei
- **Address:** 17F, Palais de Chine Hotel (君品酒店), No. 3, Sec. 1, Chengde Rd, Datong, Taipei 103
- **Phone:** +886 2 2181 9985
- **Website:** https://www.palaisdechinehotel.com/p/pdc_en/pages/lepalais
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Le+Palais+%E9%A1%A1%E5%AE%AE+Palais+de+Chine+No.+3+Sec.+1+Chengde+Rd+Taipei
- **Reviewed:** 2024-12-05
- **Author:** Christian Van Der Henst (Cvander)
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/le-palais
- **City guide:** Taipei: https://www.cookfoodie.com/wishlist/taipei

### Review

If you read the fancy duck at Mister Jiu’s in San Francisco, this is where to go fancy in Taipei. Three Michelin stars. Gorgeous room. Decor, tables, lighting. Then the food. 17F, Palais de Chine, right on Taipei Main.

Order the duck with the reservation. Two ways: 先知鴨, the young duck, smaller, soft bone, usually two eats. Or 火焰片皮鴨, the flame crispy-skin duck, three or four ways, all the parts with max flavor. Book both days ahead.

Before even booking your flight ticket to Taipei, you should check if they have an opening at Le Palais. It will improve your trip and give you an amazing impression of how refined the food in Taiwan can be.

When the duck is ready, a chef brings it to your table and starts slicing. You’ll see that ritual all over the room, each table with its own chef. After the first serves, they turn the rest into soup. You get a few choices. We also had the fried rice. Nice. Their teas are delightful.

My duck place in Taiwan. Been a couple of times for important celebrations. Always a must when bringing friends to the city. Pair it with the museum, the pork and the jade cabbage, and you get why this city is full of foodies.

Then go cheap. Night market duck: 金馥記脆皮烤鴨 in Shilin, and 真福記 in Songshan near Taipei Arena. Hotel one night, daily meal the next. What a city. Always underrated. Good for the ones who know.

Update: as of this first visit. Taïrroir also has 3 Michelin stars in 2026. Review stands as of when I went.

### Guest perspective: Taiwanese friends on Le Palais

Taiwanese friends who’d been here a few times introduced me to this place. Their take:

> Le Palais is incredible duck worthy of 3 Michelin stars. You will enjoy the decor. It’s hard to describe but definitely it’s very Chinese and refined, but also mixes with the kind of decor you will find in a prestigious French restaurant.

### What to order

- **先知鴨 / Young duck:** 先知鴨 is the smaller young duck, with softer bones, usually served two ways. Pre-order it when you reserve the table.
- **火焰片皮鴨 / Flame crispy-skin duck:** The larger showpiece: flame-finished crispy-skin duck served three or four ways. A chef slices it tableside, using the different parts for maximum flavor.
- **Duck soup:** Made from the rest of the bird after the tableside carving. Pick one of the soup preparations they offer for the remaining duck.
- **Fried rice:** A good addition after the duck courses: straightforward, comforting fried rice alongside the richer parts of the meal.
- **Tea:** Their teas are delightful and feel like part of the room and the ceremony of the meal.

### Tips

Required. Duck with the booking. Book on inline (opens 1st of month, 00:00, for next month). Pre-order the duck with the table. Smart casual.

### If you're visiting Le Palais

#### What should I order at Le Palais?

Pre-order the duck with your reservation. Choose 先知鴨, the smaller young duck usually served two ways, or 火焰片皮鴨, the flame crispy-skin duck served three or four ways and sliced tableside. Have the rest of the bird turned into one of the offered duck soups, and add the fried rice and tea.

#### How do I book Le Palais?

Reservations required. Book on inline (opens 1st of month, 00:00, for next month). Pre-order the duck with the table. Smart casual. Book both days ahead.

#### Where is Le Palais in Taipei?

17F, Palais de Chine Hotel (君品酒店), No. 3, Sec. 1, Chengde Rd, Datong, Taipei 103. 台北市大同區承德路一段3號17樓. Right on Taipei Main. Tue-Sun lunch 12:00-14:30, dinner 18:00-21:30; closed Mon.

#### Where should I go for cheaper duck in Taipei?

Then go cheap. Night market duck: 金馥記脆皮烤鴨 in Shilin, and 真福記 in Songshan near Taipei Arena. Hotel one night, daily meal the next.

## Swan Oyster Depot: Sicilian sashimi on Polk

> Swan Oyster Depot review, San Francisco: fresh seafood on Polk Street since 1912. Get the Sicilian sashimi. No reservations; expect a line.

- **Restaurant:** Swan Oyster Depot
- **City:** San Francisco
- **Neighborhood:** Polk Gulch
- **Cuisine:** Seafood
- **Rating:** 5/5
- **Price:** $$$
- **Must order:** Sicilian sashimi
- **Ideal for:** Seafood lovers seeking an authentic SF experience
- **Address:** 1517 Polk St, San Francisco, CA 94109
- **Phone:** +1-415-673-1101
- **Website:** https://swanoysterdepotrestaurant.com/
- **Instagram:** https://instagram.com/swan.oyster.official
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps?q=Swan+Oyster+Depot+San+Francisco
- **Reviewed:** 2024-11-12
- **Author:** Christian Van Der Henst (Cvander)
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/swan-oyster-depot
- **City guide:** San Francisco: https://www.cookfoodie.com/wishlist/san-francisco

### Review

I was lucky that I didn't have to wait this day, but usually, you actually have to wait a while to get there. The seafood is fresh, good quality, and if you happen to ask for a crab cocktail or the sashimi, you're definitely going to have a feast.

Great beer, great people, and a packed line to get what you need. So, happily to recommend this, and as good as it gets when you want some seafood.

### What to order

- **Sicilian sashimi:** The famous plate. Fresh is the point.
- **Crab cocktail:** Ask for a crab cocktail if you want a feast.

### Tips

No reservations -arrive before 11am to beat the line

### If you're visiting Swan Oyster Depot

#### Does Swan Oyster Depot take reservations?

No. First come, first served. Usually you wait a while. I was lucky one day and did not have to. Arrive early if you can.

#### What should I order at Swan Oyster Depot?

Ask for a crab cocktail or the sashimi and you are going to have a feast. Fresh seafood, good quality. Great beer too.

#### Is Swan Oyster Depot worth the wait?

Yes. Opened in 1912, so about 114 years. Great beer, great people, packed line. As good as it gets when you want seafood.

## San Ho Won, the michelin star korean bbq in San Francisco.

> San Ho Won review: Michelin-star Korean BBQ in San Francisco's Mission. Double-cut galbi grilled for you. Hard to book; share it with 4 to 6 people.

- **Restaurant:** San Ho Won
- **City:** San Francisco
- **Neighborhood:** Mission
- **Cuisine:** Korean
- **Rating:** 5/5
- **Price:** $$$$
- **Must order:** Double-Cut Galbi
- **Ideal for:** Groups of 4 to 6 who love Korean BBQ
- **Address:** 2170 Bryant St, San Francisco, CA 94110
- **Phone:** +1-415-814-2783
- **Website:** https://www.sanhowon.com
- **Instagram:** https://instagram.com/sanhowonsf
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps?q=San+Ho+Won+San+Francisco+Mission
- **Reservations:** https://resy.com/cities/sf/san-ho-won
- **Reviewed:** 2023-11-27
- **Author:** Christian Van Der Henst (Cvander)
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/san-ho-won
- **City guide:** San Francisco: https://www.cookfoodie.com/wishlist/san-francisco

### Review

If you love Korean BBQ, this is the fancy version in San Francisco. You will be full, you will be happy, and you can get leftover food to go. I always enjoy going with friends to a Korean barbecue, but for an upscale experience, San Ho Won is the one you're looking for if you want to impress. Not only will they make great barbecue meat for you, but their selection of beverages and add-ons is superb. If you've ever gone to a Korean barbecue and were worried about overcooking the meat or not having it at the right point, that's what San Ho Won will do for you.

Reservations are hard to get in advance unless you want to try the last serving at night, and that late seating might be a heavy meal. Still, San Ho Won is a very good deal: a Michelin-star menu, a very good selection of meat, and a reservation that is worth sharing with a group of four or even six people. Plan ahead, and sometimes check for the very last options in the schedule because they tend to open up occasionally. This is definitely a place worth visiting in San Francisco.

We did a small reel when we visited. It is a better way to appreciate the tasting menu. Check it out.

### Guest perspective: Friends on San Ho Won

Remarks from other friends I enjoyed this experience with:

> In San Ho Won the short rib was amazing. All in general was very good. It’s a different experience for Korean BBQ. Feels upper middle class while usually a BBQ experience is more a popular meal.

### What to order

- **Galbi (Korean BBQ Short Ribs):** Double-cut short ribs grilled tableside. The signature dish.
- **Egg Soufflé:** Light steamed egg.
- **Crispy Scallion Pancakes:** Crisp pajeon with scallions.
- **Korean beef ssam:** Beef in lettuce wraps.
- **Kimchi Jjigae:** Kimchi stew.

### Tips

Hard to book ahead on Resy unless you take the last seating, which can be a heavy meal. Worth sharing with 4 to 6 people.

### If you're visiting San Ho Won

#### Is San Ho Won walk-in friendly?

Walk-ins are a long shot. Reservations are hard to get in advance unless you want the last serving at night, and that late seating can be a heavy meal. Book on Resy when you can, and keep an eye on last-minute openings.

#### Is San Ho Won worth it for a group?

Yes. It is a very good deal for a Michelin-star menu: a strong selection of meat, leftovers to take home, and a reservation that is worth sharing with four or even six people. You will be full and you will be happy.

#### What makes San Ho Won special?

If you love Korean BBQ, this is the fancy version in San Francisco. The staff grill the meat for you at the table, so you are not worrying about overcooking it, and the portions are generous enough that leftover food to go is part of the night.
