## Nothing screams "jet set" more than a meal at Zass

> Just outside Positano, Zass at Il San Pietro is a romantic Michelin dinner: the view, octopus with figs, and lemon tagliatelle.

- **Restaurant:** Zass
- **City:** Positano
- **Neighborhood:** Amalfi Coast
- **Cuisine:** Italian
- **Rating:** 5/5
- **Price:** $$$$
- **Must order:** Tagliatelle with lemon, lobster, and pistachios
- **Ideal for:** A romantic fine-dining dinner just outside Positano
- **Address:** Via Laurito, 2, 84017 Positano SA, Italy
- **Phone:** +39 089 875455
- **Website:** https://www.zassrestaurant.com/
- **Instagram:** https://instagram.com/ilsanpietrodipositano
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Zass+Restaurant+Via+Laurito+2+Positano
- **Reviewed:** 2023-10-13
- **Author:** Christian Van Der Henst (Cvander)
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/zass

### Review

Nothing screams "jet set" more than a meal at Zass, located in the hotel Il San Pietro di Positano.

Just outside of Positano, this is the perfect romantic place for fine dining. The view, the location, the lovely hotel, and the beautiful presentation and flavors.

The terrace looks over the sea cliff. The restaurant grows its own vegetables in the hotel garden, and a pizza oven stands at one end. Piano music in the air, and staff who actually make you comfortable.

They offer a tasting menu with wine pairings. We skipped it and went for the pastas. We started with a fish tartare, but the true star was the octopus with figs.

And then there was pasta. The spaghetti was impeccable. The tagliatelle, infused with lemon, accented by lobster and pistachios, ranks among the best we have ever tasted. The cannelloni, rich with ricotta and basil, is not something to skip.

We finished sharing a local fish. We almost skipped dessert, then they brought candies and a mini crème brûlée I can still taste with my eyes closed.

We did a small reel when we visited. Check it out.

Thank you for the enchanting evening, Zass.

### What to order

- **Octopus with figs:** The true star of the night. Charcoal-grilled octopus with figs from the garden side of the menu.
- **Tagliatelle with lemon, lobster, and pistachios:** Lemon-infused tagliatelle with lobster and pistachios. Among the best pastas we have ever tasted.
- **Spaghetti:** Impeccable. Simple, and exactly what you want on that terrace.
- **Cannelloni with ricotta and basil:** Rich with ricotta and basil. Do not skip it for the other pastas.
- **Fish tartare:** The appetizer we started with, before the octopus took over.
- **Local fish:** We finished the savory courses sharing a local fish.
- **Mini crème brûlée:** We almost skipped dessert. Then came candies and a mini crème brûlée I can still taste with my eyes closed.

### Tips

Book through Il San Pietro. Online tables open 30 days ahead at 9am local time (2026). Smart casual: no shorts or sneakers. Groups larger than four should call.

### If you're visiting Zass

#### Is Zass the same as Zaas?

Yes. The restaurant at Il San Pietro di Positano is Zass. I wrote Zaas on the original reel; the official name is Zass.

#### Is Zass in the center of Positano?

It is just outside of Positano, at Il San Pietro in Laurito. That is the point: the view, the hotel, and a quieter cliff above the town.

#### Do I need a reservation at Zass in Positano?

Yes. Book through the hotel. Online tables open 30 days ahead at 9am local time (2026), and groups larger than four should call. It is Michelin-starred, and the terrace fills up.

#### What should I order at Zass?

If you skip the tasting menu, go for the pastas. Start with the octopus and figs. Get the lemon tagliatelle with lobster and pistachios, the spaghetti, and the cannelloni with ricotta and basil. Share a local fish, and do not skip the mini crème brûlée.

#### Is Zass only for hotel guests?

No. Outside guests can reserve. Dress smart casual: long trousers, no shorts or sneakers. The terrace over the sea cliff is the whole point.

## Mister Jiu's: always go for the Liberty duck

> Mister Jiu's: always go for the Liberty duck. $125 Peking duck banquet you pre-order. À la carte sells out. Chinatown, San Francisco.

- **Restaurant:** Mister Jiu's
- **City:** San Francisco
- **Neighborhood:** Chinatown
- **Cuisine:** Chinese-American
- **Rating:** 5/5
- **Price:** $$$$
- **Must order:** Liberty Duck
- **Ideal for:** When you want the best duck in town
- **Address:** 28 Waverly Pl, San Francisco, CA 94108
- **Phone:** +1-415-857-9688
- **Website:** https://www.misterjius.com
- **Instagram:** https://instagram.com/misterjius
- **Map:** https://maps.app.goo.gl/wbhmEBCU6ryRdSJSA
- **Reservations:** https://resy.com/cities/sf/mister-jius
- **Reviewed:** 2023-10-07
- **Author:** Christian Van Der Henst (Cvander)
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/mr-jius
- **City guide:** San Francisco: https://www.cookfoodie.com/wishlist/san-francisco

### Review

Mister Jiu's: always go for the Liberty duck.

I really like to eat duck in Chinese restaurants. Duck and rice. Maybe a soup by the side. It does not have to be fancy. When you want the best in town, head to Mister Jiu's.

Beautiful bar upstairs: Moongate Lounge. Great cocktails, beautiful decor. They also do fancy events if you get invited.

Talk about the duck. Liberty Farms, Sonoma. Pre-order it with the reservation. The treatment that makes the skin crispier. I have had my fair share of this dish, and I am still impressed by the flavor, the texture, and the crunch. The condiments. The little tortillas. Somebody will say those are not tortillas. If you were raised with them, you see them anywhere. Mix duck, condiments, veggies. Enjoy.

Now it is a $125 Peking duck banquet you can pre-order. The à la carte duck sells out. Pre-order it with the reservation.

Definitely the best restaurant in Chinatown. Sorry China Live. You are trendy and I love you too. El señor Jiu and I have some good stories.

Reserve in advance. Pre-order the duck. I repeat, go for the duck.

### What to order

- **Liberty Duck / Peking duck banquet:** Liberty Farms, Sonoma. Now a $125 Peking duck banquet you can pre-order with the reservation. The à la carte duck sells out. The treatment that makes the skin crispier. Flavor, texture, crunch. Mix it with the condiments, the veggies, and the little tortillas.

### Tips

Reserve in advance. Pre-order the duck.

### If you're visiting Mister Jiu's

#### Do I need to pre-order the duck at Mister Jiu's?

Yes. Pre-order the Liberty duck with the reservation. It is now a $125 Peking duck banquet. The à la carte duck sells out. I repeat, go for the duck.

#### What should I order at Mister Jiu's?

The Liberty duck. Liberty Farms, Sonoma. The skin, the crunch, the little tortillas. Mix duck, condiments, veggies. Enjoy.

#### Is Moongate Lounge worth it?

Beautiful bar upstairs. Great cocktails, beautiful decor. They also do fancy events if you get invited.

## Diacá: tasting menu in Cuatro Grados with grandpa

> Diacá in Cuatro Grados Norte, Guatemala City: tasting menu and brunch with grandpa. Huevitos revueltos chapines, sausage of beans. Now in Muxbal.

- **Restaurant:** Diacá
- **City:** Guatemala City
- **Neighborhood:** Cuatro Grados Norte
- **Cuisine:** Contemporary Guatemalan
- **Rating:** 5/5
- **Must order:** Huevitos revueltos chapines
- **Address:** Final 20 Calle km 8, Carretera a Muxbal, Cámara de la Construcción, Santa Catarina Pinula
- **Phone:** +502 4007-8164
- **Website:** https://www.diaca.gt/
- **Instagram:** https://www.instagram.com/diacagt/
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Diac%C3%A1+Final+20+Calle+km+8+Carretera+a+Muxbal+C%C3%A1mara+de+la+Construcci%C3%B3n+Santa+Catarina+Pinula
- **Reviewed:** 2022-12-27
- **Author:** Christian Van Der Henst (Cvander)
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/diaca

### Review

Diacá, Cuatro Grados Norte: bring grandpa to the tasting menu.

Tasting menu in Guatemala, in a beautiful location in Cuatro Grados. To try this place, I brought my grandpa. Half of the fun was to enjoy good Guatemalan food with him. And this was his first tasting menu. He asked a few times to repeat some dishes. They were confused. He also wondered if they were going to interrupt our conversation every time they brought another dish.

They do a lot of local dishes and also a brunch menu when I visited. A sausage of beans, really good eggs (huevitos revueltos chapines) and a lot of ingredients that will trigger your childhood if you were born in this country. A good tasting menu to share with international friends looking to explore la tierra de la eterna primavera.

Chef Débora Fadul is really building something special here. Diacá means de acá, from here. They later moved from the Cuatro Grados tower out to Muxbal, and made Latin America's 50 Best in 2025.

### What to order

- **Huevitos revueltos chapines:** Really good eggs from the brunch menu when I visited.
- **Sausage of beans:** A local brunch dish; one of the childhood-trigger ingredients.
- **Tasting menu:** Local dishes in a beautiful Cuatro Grados setting; good to share with international friends exploring la tierra de la eterna primavera.

### Tips

Book ahead. This review is from December 2022 at the old Cuatro Grados tower; the restaurant is now in Muxbal (Final 20 Calle km 8, Carretera a Muxbal).

### If you're visiting Diacá

#### Is Diacá good for a first tasting menu?

Yes. I brought my grandpa for his first tasting menu. Half of the fun was enjoying good Guatemalan food with him. He asked a few times to repeat some dishes, and wondered if they were going to interrupt our conversation every time they brought another dish.

#### What should I order at Diacá?

They do a tasting menu of local dishes, and when I visited they also had a brunch menu. Look for the sausage of beans and the huevitos revueltos chapines: really good eggs and ingredients that will trigger your childhood if you were born in Guatemala.

#### Where is Diacá now?

This visit was December 2022 at the Cuatro Grados tower. They later moved out to Muxbal: Final 20 Calle km 8, Carretera a Muxbal, Cámara de la Construcción, Santa Catarina Pinula. Book ahead.

Yes. Beautiful izakaya in the Mission. It really feels like Tokyo. Sake list is strong.

## Tony's Pizza Napoletana: Margherita in North Beach, Golden Boy if you just want a slice

> Tony's Pizza Napoletana: only 73 Margheritas a day in North Beach. You usually get one if you care. Golden Boy if you just want a slice.

- **Restaurant:** Tony's Pizza Napoletana
- **City:** San Francisco
- **Neighborhood:** North Beach
- **Cuisine:** Italian
- **Rating:** 4/5
- **Price:** $$$

### Review

Glad this is one of the best pizzas in America. Glad it exists in North Beach and makes San Francisco special. When I tried pizza in Napoli, I was confused, hehehe.

That said: good pizza, expensive pizza. Really good pizza. Try the specials. They only make 73 Margheritas a day. You usually get one if you care. Order a Margherita if you are in the room. I remember you cannot get that one to go. Only get pizza to go if you are walking to Washington Square and want to skip the line.

No reservations. Crowded. For sharing good pizza with friends, this is the place. Just a snack: walk a block to Golden Boy Pizza. Square slices. Really good.

In a city that will never match New York on pizza, this is our institution. Big, pricey, worth it.

### What to order

- **Margherita Pizza:** Order a Margherita if you are in the room. I remember you cannot get that one to go.
- **The Specials:** Try the specials. Really good pizza.

### Tips

### If you're visiting Tony's Pizza Napoletana

#### Can I get the Margherita to go?

I remember you cannot get that one to go. Only get pizza to go if you are walking to Washington Square and want to skip the line. They only make 73 Margheritas a day.

#### Does Tony's Pizza Napoletana take reservations?

Try booking via Yelp before assuming walk-in only. It is still crowded. For sharing good pizza with friends, this is the place.

#### What if I just want a slice?

Just a snack: walk a block to Golden Boy Pizza. Square slices. Really good.

Yes. Special ramen from the Tenderloin. The line is worth it. Their broth is special.

#### What should I order at Mensho Tokyo?

The special ramen. That is the one.

#### When is Mensho Tokyo open?

Dinner only, Tuesday through Sunday.

## Plow, the definite place for brunch in San Francisco

> Plow review: the best brunch in San Francisco, in Potrero Hill. Lemon ricotta pancakes, the Chinese breakfast when they have it. No reservations; go early.

- **Restaurant:** Plow
- **City:** San Francisco
- **Neighborhood:** Potrero Hill
- **Cuisine:** American Brunch
- **Rating:** 5/5
- **Price:** $
- **Must order:** Lemon ricotta pancakes
- **Ideal for:** Weekend brunch worth the wait
- **Address:** 1299 18th St, San Francisco, CA 94107
- **Phone:** +1-415-821-7569
- **Website:** https://www.plowsf.com
- **Instagram:** https://instagram.com/plowsf
- **Map:** https://www.google.com/maps?q=Plow+Potrero+Hill+San+Francisco
- **Reviewed:** 2016-12-06
- **Author:** Christian Van Der Henst (Cvander)
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.cookfoodie.com/reviews/plow
- **City guide:** San Francisco: https://www.cookfoodie.com/wishlist/san-francisco

### Review

Plow, the definite place for brunch in San Francisco.

Every time somebody asks me where to go for brunch, I mention Plow. I really like the place. It’s a great destination on Potrero Hill, and you’ll always find a line on a busy day. Go on a Wednesday, or get there early, and you can get in. It’s definitely worth it. Behind the bar, happy cooks are always surprising you with breakfasts: eggs, bread, and sometimes a Chinese version of breakfast. It’s always a fantastic experience. The coffee, the ambience, and the flavors. Try the different menus and see what you like.

Plow’s great. It’s worth the wait. If the line is really hard, still put your name on the list, walk to Farley’s (1315 18th St) half a block away, grab a tea or a coffee, and come back. I’ve had some of the best conversations in that line. If you’re lucky, you’re just getting in. I still remember during the pandemic they kept serving breakfast. I’m not sure about delivery, but I remember picking up directly. They always handed over those packages with a great smile and a lot of thanks. Plow is where you go for breakfast and really enjoy it. That’s why San Francisco has spots that are worth it. This is my best example.

Try to avoid weekends. It’s super crowded. Get there early on a weekday and you’ll have the best experience.

### What to order

- **The Plow:** Two eggs, two lemon ricotta pancakes, plow potatoes, and house sausage. This is the plate.
- **Lemon ricotta pancakes:** House made ricotta, lemon curd, salted whipped butter, pure maple syrup.
- **Grain bowl:** Quinoa, black rice, Hodo Soy yuba, kale, oyster mushrooms, soy marinated egg. Avocado when you add it.
- **Two egg brekkie:** Eggs with house made pork sausage, plow potatoes, and toast.
- **Hong Kong style toast:** Lightly burnt brioche, coffee condensed milk, sea salt.
- **Chinese breakfast (when available):** Ask if they have it. Not always on the menu.

### Tips

No reservations. Stick to weekdays; get there early. If the line is hard, put your name down and walk to Farley's (1315 18th St) for coffee.

### If you're visiting Plow

#### How do I deal with the line at Plow?

Try to avoid weekends. Go on a Wednesday or get there early on a weekday. If the line is really hard, put your name on the list, walk to Farley's (1315 18th St) half a block away, grab a tea or coffee, and come back.

#### Is Plow worth the wait?

Yes. Every time somebody asks me where to go for brunch, I mention Plow. Worth it.

#### What should I order at Plow?

Eggs, bread, whatever they are surprising you with behind the bar. Sometimes a Chinese version of breakfast. Try the different menus and see what you like.
